title: Certificates of Deposit: which penalty entry is checked for a wrong rate or wrong penalty days
content:
## Scope

When a Certificates of Deposit certificate's early withdrawal penalty is checked for having been booked at a rate or a number of penalty days other than the charter's, this rule fixes which penalty entry is examined and where each figure of the check is read from.

## Rule

1. The penalty checked is the certificate's most recent early withdrawal penalty entry, by posted date.
2. Its amount, the rate applied, the penalty days and the posted date are all read from that one entry. Figures are never mixed across two penalty entries.
3. An earlier penalty is checked under this rule only while it is the certificate's most recent penalty. Once a later penalty has been posted, the earlier one is left to the bank's general penalty reversal rules.
4. **Current term only.** The check applies to a penalty taken in the certificate's current term, that is, one whose posted date is on or after the certificate's term start date, because the rate the check rebuilds is the rate of the current term. A penalty taken in an earlier term is left to the bank's general penalty reversal rules.

## Input, judgement, output

| Input | Judgement | Output |
|---|---|---|
| All early withdrawal penalty entries on the certificate | Which has the latest posted date? | The one entry under check |
| That entry | Read its amount, rate applied, penalty days and posted date | The four figures used in the check |

## Illustrative case (hypothetical entries)

A certificate carries two penalty entries: one posted 3 March for 42.10 at 90 days, and one posted 20 June for 18.75 at 180 days.

- The entry checked is the 20 June entry. Its amount is 18.75, its penalty days 180, its posted date 20 June, and its rate applied is the rate shown on that same entry.
- The 3 March entry is not checked under this rule, because it is no longer the most recent penalty; it falls under the general penalty reversal rules.
- Reading the 180 days from the June entry together with the 42.10 from the March entry would be a wrong reading: all four figures come from one entry.
- The June entry is checked here only if the certificate's current term started on or before 20 June. Had the current term started on 1 July, the June entry, although still the most recent penalty, would belong to an earlier term and would be left to the general penalty reversal rules.

## Points of judgement

**The customer points to an older penalty and says that one was wrong. Is it checked here?**
Only while it is the certificate's most recent penalty. If a later penalty has been posted since, the older penalty is left to the general penalty reversal rules.
